body:
WHAT
When the TEST button asks a server for its model list (GET /models) and gets 404, the app does not guess what that means. It sends a deliberately invalid POST to /chat/completions on the same base URL: 400, 422 or 200 means the chat route exists (server just has no catalog), 401 or 403 means it exists but refused the key, and 404 or 405 means this URL is not the API at all.

WHY
A server with no /models catalog and a wrong base URL both answer 404 on /models. Treating that as 'reachable' made TEST pass on a URL that could never chat, and sent the user off to check an API key that was fine.

WHERE
app/main/connection.js — testEndpoint() (the `res.status === 404 || res.status === 405` branch inside the candidate loop) calls probeChatRoute(baseUrl, headers, timeoutMs, fetchImpl, insecureTls), which returns "exists" | "unauthorized" | "missing"; the verdict decides between { ok: true, note: "server reachable — it has no /models catalog…" }, recording an authFailure, or moving to the next candidate URL.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. With a fake fetchImpl that answers 404 on /models and 400 on POST /chat/completions, testEndpoint returns ok:true with models:[] and a note about the missing /models catalog, and baseUrl equal to the probed candidate.
2. With 404 on /models and 422 (or 200) on the chat route, the result is also ok:true — every non-404/405/401/403 answer counts as 'route exists'.
3. With 404 on /models and 401 on the chat route for every candidate, testEndpoint returns ok:false with status 401 and an error saying the endpoint rejected the API key (the URL is right, check the key).
4. With 404 on /models and 404 (or 405) on the chat route for every candidate, the result is ok:false with the 'no OpenAI-compatible API found at that address' error and no auth blame.
5. The chat-route probe is a POST with Content-Type application/json and body {model:"", messages:[]}; a fetch that throws on the probe is treated as 'missing' and the walk continues to the next candidate.
